overview: Circuit breakers are pre-defined, automatic halts to trading activity triggered by specific loss thresholds or behavioral patterns. They are not discretionary decisions — they are rules that execute automatically when conditions are met. Their purpose is to protect capital from the compounding damage of emotional trading during adverse conditions.

daily_loss_limit.threshold_description: 3% of account equity at the start of the trading day
daily_loss_limit.example: If opening equity = $10,000, daily loss limit = $300. When cumulative realized losses for the day reach $300, the circuit breaker triggers.

trigger_action.immediate: All pending orders cancelled. No new trade signals issued for the remainder of the calendar day.
trigger_action.agent_behavior: The agent enters DAILY_HALT state. Any request for a new trade signal returns: 'CIRCUIT BREAKER ACTIVE: Daily loss limit of 3% reached. No new signals until next trading day. Focus: review trades, identify edge deviation, prepare for next session.'
trigger_action.logging: Trigger event logged with timestamp, trades that contributed to the loss, and whether losses resulted from valid edge trades or rule violations.
trigger_action.reset: Circuit breaker resets at the start of the next trading day (00:00 UTC or defined session open).

daily_loss_limit.rationale: A 3% daily loss is significant but recoverable. Allowing further trading after a 3% loss — especially in an emotionally activated state — risks compounding the loss to an account-threatening level. Stopping preserves capital and psychological stability.

weekly_loss_limit.threshold_description: 5% of account equity at the start of the trading week
weekly_loss_limit.example: If week opening equity = $10,000, weekly loss limit = $500. When cumulative realized losses for the week reach $500, the circuit breaker triggers.

trigger_action.immediate: All trading halted for the remainder of the calendar week.
trigger_action.agent_behavior: The agent enters WEEKLY_HALT state. Returns: 'CIRCUIT BREAKER ACTIVE: Weekly loss limit of 5% reached. Trading suspended until the start of next week. Mandatory: conduct full weekly review per recalibration protocol.'
trigger_action.mandatory_review: Before trading resumes the following week, the agent must conduct a full weekly recalibration review (see weekly_recalibration section).
trigger_action.reset: Circuit breaker resets at the start of the next trading week after recalibration review is completed.

weekly_loss_limit.interaction_with_daily_limit: A weekly loss limit trigger may occur before the daily limit is reached if losses accumulate across multiple days. Both limits are tracked independently and simultaneously.
weekly_loss_limit.rationale: A 5% weekly loss signals that market conditions may have shifted adversely or that execution has deviated from the edge. A full week off allows conditions to stabilize and the agent to recalibrate before risking further capital.

consecutive_loss_cooldown.description: After 3 consecutive closed losing trades, the agent enters a 24-hour cooldown period regardless of daily or weekly loss amounts.
consecutive_loss_cooldown.calculation: Consecutive losses are counted from the most recent closed trade backward. A single winning trade resets the consecutive loss counter to zero.

trigger_action.immediate: Signal generation suspended for 24 hours from the time of the third consecutive loss.
trigger_action.agent_behavior: Enters CONSECUTIVE_LOSS_COOLDOWN state. Returns: 'CIRCUIT BREAKER ACTIVE: 3 consecutive losses detected. 24-hour cooldown initiated. Time remaining: [X] hours. Recommended action: review the three losing trades for edge adherence.'
trigger_action.review_requirement: During the 24-hour cooldown, a mini-review of the three losing trades must be conducted: Were edge criteria properly met? Was stop placement correct? Was position sizing correct? Did market conditions change during the trade?
trigger_action.reset: 24 hours after trigger time, trading resumes with a fresh consecutive loss counter.

consecutive_loss_cooldown.rationale: Three consecutive losses can indicate: (1) a genuine losing streak within normal distribution — the edge is intact, (2) a change in market regime making the edge temporarily ineffective, or (3) execution errors or rule deviations. A 24-hour pause forces investigation before further capital is risked.
consecutive_loss_cooldown.important_note: This circuit breaker is NOT triggered by the size of losses — only by the count of consecutive losses. Three small losing trades each at 0.5% risk triggers the same cooldown as three large losing trades.

revenge_trading_prevention.definition: Revenge trading is the act of placing additional trades immediately after a loss with the primary motivation of recovering the lost capital rather than executing a valid edge setup. It is driven by ego and loss aversion rather than analysis. It is one of the most destructive patterns in trading psychology.

time_proximity_flag.description: If a new trade signal is requested within 15 minutes of closing a losing trade, the agent flags this as a potential revenge trading trigger.
time_proximity_flag.agent_action: Before issuing the signal, the agent must output: 'REVENGE TRADING CHECK: A trade was closed at a loss [X] minutes ago. Confirm this signal meets all edge criteria and is not emotionally motivated.' Agent then proceeds only if all edge criteria are met.

size_escalation_flag.description: If a trade signal is requested with a position size larger than the standard formula output, the agent flags this as a potential revenge trading attempt.
size_escalation_flag.agent_action: Reject the oversized signal immediately. Output: 'SIGNAL REJECTED: Requested position size exceeds formula output. Revenge trading prevention protocol active. Standard size applied.' Agent recalculates with correct size.

below_threshold_override_flag.description: If a trade is requested on a setup with a confidence score below the minimum threshold after a losing trade, the agent flags this as a potential revenge trading attempt.
below_threshold_override_flag.agent_action: Reject the signal. Output: 'SIGNAL REJECTED: Setup does not meet minimum confidence threshold. Post-loss low-quality signal rejected under revenge trading prevention protocol.'

rapid_sequential_signals_flag.description: If 3 or more trade signals are requested within a 2-hour window after a loss, the agent flags this as a potential revenge trading pattern.
rapid_sequential_signals_flag.agent_action: After the third signal request in the window, output: 'PATTERN WARNING: 3+ trade signals requested within 2 hours of a loss. This pattern is associated with revenge trading. Mandatory 30-minute cooling period before the next signal will be processed.'

revenge_trading_prevention.core_principle: The agent does not have emotions. However, it serves a human trader who does. The revenge trading prevention architecture protects the human from their own emotional state during a vulnerable period. The architecture assumes that the human may not recognize they are in a revenge trading state — the agent provides the objective check.

weekly_recalibration.trigger: End of each trading week (mandatory) or upon weekly loss limit circuit breaker trigger (mandatory before resuming).
weekly_recalibration.description: A structured review process that evaluates the past week's trading performance against the edge and risk management rules to identify deviations, validate the edge, and prepare for the next week.

required_review_items.description: Review each trade: were all edge criteria met? Was stop placed correctly? Was position sizing formula applied? Were targets used? Flag any violations.
Calculate the week's realized expectancy in R-multiples. Compare against historical expectancy baseline. Flag significant negative divergence.
Were any circuit breakers triggered? If yes, what trades triggered them? Were those trades rule-compliant or rule-violating? Update the incident log.
Assess whether the market regime (trending, ranging, volatile, low-volatility) matches the conditions the edge was validated in. If regime has shifted, reduce risk percentage for next week.
If win rate has diverged more than 15 percentage points below historical average over the past 30 trades, flag for edge re-evaluation. Consider reducing position size to 0.5% risk while monitoring.
Update the account equity figure used in all position sizing formulas. Always use current equity, never last week's equity.
Identify key levels (major S/R zones, upcoming high-impact news events, significant Fibonacci levels) for the next week. Prepare the analysis framework before the week begins.

weekly_recalibration.output_requirement: The weekly recalibration must produce a written summary including: (1) rules adherence rate, (2) realized expectancy in R, (3) any circuit breaker incidents, (4) market regime assessment, (5) next week risk level (standard or reduced), and (6) key levels watchlist.
